author: opt-B1det

contract.sync_assumed: caller separates consecutive calls that reuse the temp storage by a block barrier
contract.sync_performed: __syncthreads inside: 2 per radix pass plus 1 init, plus 1 in the tie phase when the candidates at the k-th key exceed the remaining k
contract.n_range: N = Threads x IPT, IPT 1 to 64 under prefer_smaller_index (the tie decision is a 64-bit mask per thread), measured 1024, 4096 and 16384 at 256 threads and 32768 at 512 threads, N 32768 at 256 threads is unsupported
contract.type_constraints: fp32 and bf16 through the radix traits, int32 indices derived from the striped tile position
contract.nan_behavior: NaN twiddles to the largest radix key and is selected first, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 is normalized to +0.0 once in the prologue so both zeros form one tie class
contract.tie_break_support: inherent under prefer_smaller_index: warp-redundant rank (knowledge base 4.5 approach C) over the exact ties after the last pass, index order on striped tiles, taken ties written at total_selected + rank. The emission ticket of the strictly selected items is one shared atomic per item on a class-indexed counter (B1_idx's spelling, T57), the ties draw and drop a ticket on the second counter. Price against B1_idx under not_guaranteed in the same session: fp32 (no ties at rank k) within 1 percent latency at N 1024 and 4096, 3.5 to 9.6 percent at N 16384, bf16 5 to 10 percent at N 1024, 12 to 24 at N 4096, 12 to 37 at N 16384, see findings
contract.sorted_output_support: not supported inherently, post-sort of k

correctness_notes: 18 prefer_smaller_index cells at N 1024, 4096 and 16384 (256 threads, label d2b) and 6 at N 32768 with 512 threads (label d2c), 27 oracle cases per cell including the five signed_zero seeds, signed_zero_boundary and pivot_tie_zero with the exact index check, all passed for the variant, the control B1_idx checked for set validity under not_guaranteed. Control B1_idx instantiated under not_guaranteed in the same process and lock section (harness 0.8 --control-req), so the number is the price of the requirement. The 6 cells at N 32768 and 256 threads are unsupported (IPT 128 exceeds the 64-bit tie mask), the 512-thread cells of the same N carry threads 512 in the cell and their control is B1_idx at 512 threads. The before figures quoted in the findings are the verified card B1_det_b200_20261025_1 (same control, same node, constant-address ticket).

low_level: B1_det2 against B1_idx under not_guaranteed at fp32 N 1024 k 16: 1240 against 992 SASS instructions in the latency kernel, the difference is the tie phase (8 VOTE.ANY, 8 POPC, 8 SHFL.IDX, 4 more SHFL.UP and 2 more BAR.SYNC over two copies of the primitive) plus the -0.0 normalization (one ISETP and one SEL per item). Both ticket sites are the same plain per-item ATOMS.ADD on a class-indexed register address, 8 each, no S2R SR_LTMASK in either kernel. bf16 904 against 656. Registers of the latency kernel 40 against 32 at IPT 4, 64 against 47 or 48 at IPT 16, 206 to 209 against 128 at IPT 64: resolve_ties keeps one ballot word and one rank word per item slot across the tie barrier and into the epilogue plus the 64-bit taken mask. Throughput kernel 40 against 32 at fp32 IPT 4 (6 against 8 blocks per SM), 32 against 32 at bf16 (8 both), 61 to 64 against 42 to 47 at IPT 16 (4 against 5), 207 to 227 against 122 to 128 at IPT 64 (1 against 2). No STL, LDL or stack frame in any 256-thread cell.

At 512 threads and N 32768 (IPT 64, the only form of N 32768 under the 64-bit tie mask) the launch bound caps B1_det2 at 128 registers and the tie arrays go to local memory: stack 216 bytes, 592 spill bytes with 74 STL and 74 LDL in the latency kernel, 424 bytes with 53 and 53 in the throughput kernel (run.py flags the cells LOCAL, the T36 check), while B1_idx at 512 threads holds 100 to 104 registers with no spill.

Phase stamps (T56 method, approaches/B1/profile_det_phases.cu, one block, median of 32 calls on random normal rows, state/results/opt-B1det/prof/profile_165917.log, the same header with the deterministic path on and off): the tie phase costs 192 + 334 = 526 cycles per run at IPT 4 (ballots, table stores and barrier, then the base scan and per-slot ranks), 433 + 571 = 1004 at IPT 16 and 1546 + 1459 = 3005 at IPT 64, and it ran in 9 of 32 rows at bf16 N 1024 k 16, 12 of 32 at k 256, 21 of 32 at N 4096 k 64 and 29 of 32 at N 16384 k 256, never on fp32. The -0.0 normalization plus pass 1 (no barrier separates them for thread 0) costs 14 more cycles at IPT 4, 67 at IPT 16 and 330 (fp32) to 554 (bf16) at IPT 64. The B1_det2 epilogue is cheaper than B1_idx's by 42 (bf16 N 1024 k 16), 119 (k 256), 236 (N 4096 k 64) and 681 cycles (N 16384 k 256), B1_idx's bounded tie store costs more instructions per item than the class branch, but 463 more at fp32 N 16384 k 16.
algorithmic: Price of prefer_smaller_index with the class-indexed ticket (B1_det2 against B1_idx under not_guaranteed, same lock section, latency in cycles per call and throughput in Gelem per s). fp32, no ties at rank k, the tie phase never runs: latency minus 0.7 to plus 1.0 percent at N 1024 and 4096 (1802 against 1807 at k 16, 1915 against 1914, 2144 against 2152, 3714 against 3675, 4631 against 4638, 5198 against 5232), plus 9.6, 6.3 and 3.5 percent at N 16384 (9809 against 8953, 11407 against 10736, 13705 against 13243), plus 9.2, 6.9 and 5.0 at N 32768 with 512 threads (13034 against 11938, 15415 against 14426, 16917 against 16119). Throughput plus 5.2, 4.3 and 3.2 percent at N 1024 (392 against 412), plus 11.1, 9.3 and 6.5 at N 4096 (624 against 693), plus 82, 77 and 74 at N 16384 (379 against 691, one block per SM against two), plus 9.1, 7.8 and 4.6 at N 32768 with 512 threads (607 against 663).

bf16, 1.4 to 11.2 ties at rank k on average: latency plus 5.2, 7.8 and 10.3 percent at N 1024 k 16, 64 and 256 (1868 against 1775, 2028 against 1881, 2179 against 1976), plus 12.2, 24.3 and 22.5 at N 4096 (3790 against 3377, 4779 against 3845, 5529 against 4512), plus 12.1, 25.3 and 36.7 at N 16384 (9962 against 8890, 11810 against 9424, 15263 against 11170), plus 27.4, 51.2 and 53.1 at N 32768 with 512 threads (16848 against 13222, 20453 against 13528, 22340 against 14591). Throughput plus 12.6 to 14.7 percent at N 1024 (362 against 408), 22 to 39 at N 4096 (567 against 692), 71 to 100 at N 16384 (372 against 636), 23 to 43 at N 32768 (475 against 584).

Before, card B1_det_b200_20261025_1 (constant-address ticket, same control, same node, verified): fp32 latency plus 19.2, 19.3 and 12.9 percent at N 1024 and plus 22.8, 23.9 and 25.6 at N 4096, bf16 plus 23.2, 25.6 and 22.3 at N 1024 and plus 34.3, 51.1 and 48.2 at N 4096, throughput plus 8 to 62 percent. The ticket spelling was the whole fp32 price at N 1024 and 4096 and 14 to 27 points of the bf16 price. What remains is the tie phase on the rows where the items equal to the k-th key exceed the remaining slots, the normalization at IPT 64, and the registers of the tie arrays at IPT 64 and above.

The tie phase is per item slot, not per tie: ballots, table stores, base shuffles and rank popcounts run for every slot (64 of each per thread at IPT 64, issue bound at 2 warps per scheduler through the VOTE and SHFL pipes, T33), and the phase runs whenever the ties do not exactly fill the remaining slots, which is 28 percent of the rows at bf16 N 1024 k 16 and 91 percent at N 16384 k 256. Expected cost per call from the profile, run fraction times 526, 1004 or 3005 cycles plus the normalization minus the cheaper epilogue: about 100 cycles at bf16 N 1024 k 16 (harness 93), 740 at N 4096 k 64 (harness 934), 3150 at N 16384 k 256 (harness 4093). The knowledge base 4.5 figure of about 1 percent for the warp-redundant rank holds at bf16 N 1024 k 16 within a factor of five and nowhere above.

The register price at IPT 64 is a second, independent term: the deterministic path keeps 2 x IPT words (ballots and ranks) plus the mask across the tie barrier, 206 to 227 registers against 122 to 128, so the throughput kernel runs one block per SM instead of two (minus 42 to 50 percent throughput at fp32 N 16384 where no tie phase ever runs) and the 512-thread form spills.
negative: The residual price at IPT 64 is not the ticket and not the tie phase alone: fp32 N 16384 pays 3.5 to 9.6 percent latency and 74 to 82 percent throughput with no tie at rank k, the register footprint of the tie arrays and the IPT 64 normalization (330 cycles).
The per-slot tie phase does not pay at N 4096 and above for bf16: 1004 to 3005 cycles per run, a third to two thirds of a radix pass at that N, for 1.7 to 11 tied items per row.
surprises: At fp32 N 1024 and 4096 the deterministic path is within noise of the not_guaranteed path in latency although it carries the -0.0 normalization (B1_nz measured 25 to 31 cycles for it at N 1024) and the tie barrier that never runs, the normalization hides in the dependency-bound prologue and the stamps put it at 14 cycles at IPT 4.

The B1_det2 epilogue is cheaper than the not_guaranteed epilogue of B1_idx by 42 to 681 cycles for bf16 (the class branch against the bounded tie store), so part of the bf16 tie phase is paid back there, while at fp32 N 16384 k 16 the det2 epilogue costs 463 more with the same code, a register allocation effect at 249 registers in the profile build that was not traced.
open_questions: Whether a per-candidate rank lookup from shared tables (store the full ballot word per warp and slot instead of its popcount, write the per-slot bases of the shuffle scan to shared memory, then let only the threads with a candidate loop over their set mask bits and read base and ballot, no tie_rank or ballots array in registers, no per-slot shuffles) brings the tie scan phase from 334 to 1459 cycles down to the scan alone and restores two blocks per SM at IPT 64, idea card ideas/queue/B1_det3_candidate_rank_lookup.md.

Whether a one-ballot any-candidate test per warp lets most warps skip the per-slot ballot and table loop (the ties sit in 2 or 3 of 8 warps on random rows), the ballot phase is 192 to 1546 cycles per run.
The 463-cycle epilogue difference at fp32 N 16384 k 16 in the profile build, and whether the T512 spill of the tie arrays goes away with the lookup form.
